newsitem.title: UK: UK's Clarke "not mad set" on joining EMU.
newsitem.headline: UK's Clarke "not mad set" on joining EMU.

text.p: Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said he was "not mad set" on Britain joining a single European currency and had a genuinely open mind on the subject.
"I'm not mad set on this country joining a single currency," he said in a BBC radio interview.
Clarke, the leading Europhile in the cabinet, said Conservative "Euro-sceptics" had parodied his views.

"Because I say we should keep our option open, that it would be silly of us just to walk away from it and leave the discussion to the others, because I say it might be to the advantage of this country to join it at some time, Euro-sceptics say I'm a federalist and secretly, desperately wanting to join the single currency," he said.
He said single currency membership could have advantages, including for importers and exporters: "But it could have serious disadvantages."

"This country is in the happy position, thanks to John Major at Maastricht, in that we can sit back, get properly involved in the planning of it, and eventually make our minds up whether we want to join."
He said he was against a federal Europe and had met very few people who were in favour.
"Euro-sceptics who don't know much about Europe call everybody who has ever crossed the Channel a federalist. But this is nonsense. Nobody's planning a federal Europe, whatever that may mean."

Clarke said the way Britain left the Exchange Rate Mechanism had been a "debacle" and he dismissed the Euro-sceptic claim that Britain started to recover from recession only because it left the ERM as a myth.
